lawyer:
Md Mahbub Ali with Sk Habib-ul-Alam, Advocates -----For the Petitioner. 
Md Mozammel Hossain, Advocate ----- For the Opposite Party Nos: 1-2.
parties:
Monoruddin (Md) ----- Plaintiff-Appellant-Petitioner
Vs
Md. Salauddin Sarkar and others ----- Defendant-Respondent-Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-4 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 26-7-2011 and 1-8-2011 respectively passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur in Other Class Appeal No. 140 of 2008 disallowing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 21- 10-2008 and 28-10-2008 respectively passed by the Assistant Judge, 4fh Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 249 of 2006 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The fact of the case lies in a very short compass. The petitioner as plaintiff filed title Suit No. 249 of 2006 in the Court of 4th Assistant Judge, Gazipur, for a decree of permanent injunction against the defendant opposite parties, stating, inter alia, that the suit lands originally belonged to Hazmat Ali and accordingly, recorded in his name in CS Khatian No. 124. Hazmat Ali sold out 0.90 sataks of land out of 1.11 acres in CS plot No. 359 and 0.06 acres in CS plot No. 360 totalling 0.96 acres to his son Mohammad Ali by a registered deed No. 7083 dated 7-10-1942. Mohammad Ali sold 0.171/2sataks out of 0.90 sataks from plot No. 359 to Bhaira Lal Ruhidash. The said Bhaira Lal Ruhidash again sold out the said 0.171/2sataks to Ayeb Ali and others vide registered deed No. 13892 dated 6-12-1948. Then Ayeb Ali and others sold the. Saido.17 and 1/2 sataks land to the plaintiff Md Monoruddin vide registered deed No. 4808 dated 11-4-1970. Mohammad Ali again sold 0.12 sataks of land out of 0.72 and 1/2 sataks to one Mokles Uddin Mia vide registered deed No. 8642 dated 17-4-1961, 0.17 and 1/2sataks to the plaintiff Mdonoruddin by registered deed No. 138 dated 2-1-1,967 and 0.17 and 1/2sataks to Lal Mia vide registered deed No. 3087 dated 6-2-1961. So, after the transfers aforesaid Mohammad Ali had 25 and1/2sataks of land in plot No. 359 under CS khatian No. 124. Hazmat Ali died leaving behind 2 (two) sons namely, Mohammad Ali and Ohad Ali and 3 (three) daughters, Moziran Nessa, Asia Khatun and Alemon Nessa. From remaining 21 sataks land in plot No. 359 each son got 0.06 sataks and each daughter got 0.03 sataks. Among the aforesaid sons and daughters of Hazmat Ali, .Ohad Ali and Moziran Nessa sold 0.06 + 0.03 = 0.09 sataks land to the plaintiff vide registered deed No. 5788 dated 22-5-1967 and another two daughters Asia Khatun and AlemonNessa sold their 0.03 + 0.03 = 0.06 sataks land to the plaintiff vide registered deed No. 9219 dated 8-9-1969. Moklesuddin sold 0.12 sataks land in plot No. 359 to the plaintiff vide registered deed No. 3385 dated 1.6-3-1970 and deed No. 8642 dated 17-4-196L After the transfers Mohammad Ali had 25 and 1/2sataks in plot No. 159 and 0.06 sataks in plot No. 360 and accordingly for the said quantum of land RS record has been prepared in his name. He died leaving' behind son Shahajuddin and daughter Tara Banu. Thereafter, Tara Banu sold 0.09 sataksvide registered deed No. 6187 dated 6-6-1967 and 0.09 sataks vide deed No. 7322 dated 24-7-1967 to the plaintiff but handed over possession of 0.121/2sataks land. Shahajuddin sold 0.25 sataks land to the plaintiff vide registered deed No. 2067 dated 19-2-1970. Accordingly, the plaintiff has become owner of 0.99 and 1/2sataks land covered by plot Nos. 359 and 360 by purchase: The plaintiff sold 0.58 sataks land out of 0.991/2sataks to the different persons and he has been owning and possessing 0.41 and 1/2sataks land. The defendant has mutated his name in the khatian by filing Mutation Case No. 7005/1999-2000 and 5005/2001-2002 on the basis of a fabricated deed No. 22684 dated 11- 12- 2001 alleged tohave been executed by one Alauddin who had no title in the suit property. The Plaintiff upon receipt of information about the same prayed for cancellation of the alleged mutation cases before the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Gazipur, by filing a Miscellaneous Case No.4 7 of 2002. The Assistant Commissioner (Land), advised the plaintiff to go to civil court for prop relief. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 259 of 2003 which was renumbered as Title Suit No.7 of 2005 but for some mistake in the plaint, he has withdrawn the said suit for filing a fresh suit. The defendant threatened the plaintiff with dispossession and tried to take over possession of the suit land on 2- 9-2005 at 9-00 am. Hence, the instant suit for permanent injunction.

3. The opposite party No.1 as defendant contested the suit by filing written, statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the land in CS khatian No. 124 originally belonged to Hazmat Ali. He died leaving behind only son Mohammad AIL Mohammad Ali died leaving behind son Alauddin and daughter Tara Banu. Mohammad Ali has/had no son named Shahajuddin. The said Alauddin and Tara Banu while owning and' possessing the land they sold 0.60 sataks to the defendant No. 1 vide registered deed No. 22683 dated 11-12-2001 and on the same date they sold 0.06 sataks land vide registered Deed No. 22864 totaling 0.66 sataks to the defendant No. 1 and handed over possession of the same. Mohammad Ali never sold his land in his life time to anybody. Alauddin sold a portion of the suit plots to the defendant No.1 by registered deed and exchanged 0,06sataks with the defendant No.1. The defendant' No.1 after purchase got his name mutated vide case No. 5005/2001-2002 and paid rent upto 1411 BS and possessing the suit land, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. The plaintiff examined 4 (four) witnesses and defendant examined none to-prove his case.

5. The trial court upon contested hearing dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 21-10-2008. Against the judgment of the trial court, the plaintiff-petitioner preferred Other Class Appeal No. 140 of 2008 before the District Judge, Gazipur and the said appeal was heard by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court; Gazipur on transfer, who upon contested hearing disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree of the trial court. At this stage, the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of status-quo. During pendency of this revision the petitioner died and his heirs have been substituted.

6. Mr Md Mahbub Ali, senior Advocate, with, Mr Sk Habib-ul-Alam, the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners submit that the petitioner successfully proved the case before the trial court by adducing sufficient evidences both oral and documentary relating to the suit property and even by amending the plaint in appeal but both the courts below upon misconception of law as well as misreading Of the evidences on record most illegally dismissed the suit as well as the appeal. He further submits that the defendants though filed a written statement denying the case of the plaintiff but at the time Of hearing did not adduce any evidence even produced a single paper before the trial court in support of his claim and, as such, the defendant-opposite party has no case before the court in accordance with law. It is also argued that the petitioner categorically stated his case in the plaint as well as' at the time of recording deposition and produced witnesses in support of their possession in the suit property but both the courts below upon misconstruction of the evidences adduced before the trial court most illegally dismissed the suit 'of the plaintiff as well as the appeal on the finding that the plaintiff could not prove their possession and title in the suit property by producing sufficient evidences both, oral and documentary and, as such, the judgments and decree of the' courts  below is liable to be set-aside

7. Mr Md Mozaminel Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party Nos.1 and 2 submits that the suit was filed by the plaintiff seeking a decree against the defendant. The cardinal principal of law is that the plaintiff is to prove his case by adducing and producing sufficient evidences before the trial court and he cannot depend upon the weakness of the defence; But in the instant case the petitioner as plaintiff could not prove, his case by filing sufficient documents in support of his alleged title and also failed to prove his exclusive, possession in the suit land and, as such, both the courts below rightly dismissed the suit as well as the appeal and by refusing the prayer of the petitioner, both-the courts below have not committed any error of law, resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

8. Heard the learned Advocate for the parties, gone through the application, judgments of both the courts below and the evidences lying in the lower court records.

9. Admittedly the property in question covered by two CS plot Nos. 359 arid 360 under CS Khatian No. 124 measuring 1.17acres originally belonged to one Hazmat Ali, who by areglistered deed dated 7-10-1942 transferred 90 sataks of land from Plot Nos: 359 (part) and 360 (full) to his son Mohammad Aliand thesaid Mohammad Ali by different kabalas of different dates transferred total quantum of landmeasuring  64 and 1/2   sataksout of his purchased 0.90 sataks land. The remaining 21 sataks of plot No. 359 left by Hazmat Ali were inherited by his son Mohammad Ali and Ohad Ali, three daughters namely, Mojiran Nessa, Asia Khatun and Alemon Nessa; The petitioner claimed that he purchased the suit land from Mohammad Ali, his brother, sisters and his :son Shahajuddin and daughter Tara Banu on differentdates by different kabala stotalling 0.99 and 1/2sataks. Out of the purchased land the petitioner transferred 0.58 sataks of land to different persons who have been possessing the same with specific boundary.

10. The opposite parties claimed that Hazmat Ali had only son named Mohammad Ali He had no other heirs named Ohad Ali, Mojiran Nessa, Asia Khatun and Alemon Nessa. Mohammad Ali died leaving son Alauddin and daughter Tara Banu.: The opposite party claimed that they got 0.06 sataks of land from Plot No. 359 by way of exchange with the son and daughter Mohammd Ali and after exchange they got their names mutated in the khatian and possessing the same on payment of regular rents to the Government. On the other hand, the petitioners claimed that Mohammad Ali died leaving son Shahajuddin and Tara Banu who got 0.37 nad 1/2 sataks of land by inheritance and sold the same to the petitioner in the year 1967 and by purchase the petitioners have been possessing the suit land with specific boundary. The petitioner in support of his claim adduced 4 witnesses including the petitioner's son.

11. It appears from the examination-in-chief that PW 1 chronologically stated the case of the petitioner with reference, to the deeds of transfer. PWs 2, 3 and 4 deposed in respect of possession of the petitioner. The plaintiff-petitioner to prove his title in the property produced some documents which were duly exhibited as Exhibits-2-8. In cross-examination by the defendant opposite parties, PWs told that Hazmat Ali had two sons and three daughters and Mohammad Ali died leaving son Shahujuddin and daughter Tara Banu and denied the suggestion that Hazmat Ali had only son Mohammad Ali.

12. I have gone through the judgment of the trial court. It appears that the trial court chronologically stated the case of the plaintiff and considered the exhibits filed by the petitioner and also considered the written statement filed by the opposite parties as defendant but the trial court in its judgment observed that though the defendant- opposite parties filed written statement and cross- examined the PWs giving suggestions but did not adduce any evidence both oral and documentary and observed that the defendants claim has no basis at all. The trial court upon consideration of the evidences and the documents filed by the petitioner came to a finding that:

বাদীপক্ষ দাবী করে যে বিভিন্ন দলিল মূলে ক্রয়সূত্রে এবং ১/২ শতাংশ সম্পতিতে মালিক দখলদার থাকা কালে ৫৮ শতাংশ জমি বিভিন্ন লোকের বরাবর হস্তান্তর করে দখল বুঝিয়ে দিয়ে বাকী ৪১ এবং ১/২ শতাংশ জমির ভোগ দখলকার আছেন। বাদীর দাখিলী প্রর্দশনী চিহিূত  দলিল সূত্রে বাদীর ৪০ শতাংশ জমিতে মালিক থাকা প্রমানিত হলে ও দাবীকৃত বাকী জমির মালিকানা বিষয়ে উপযুক্ত প্রমাণ দাখিল হয়নি। তাছাড়া বাদী তার মালিকানাধীন কোন দাগ বা খতিয়ানের কতটুকু জমি, কি সুত্রে কার বরাবর হস্থান্তর করেছে তার বণর্না বাদীর আর্জিতে উল্লেখ করেনি।

বাদী ৩১৪ নং RS খতিয়ান ভূক্ত ৪৯৫ দাগে ৬০ শতাংশ জমির কাতে ৩৫ এবং ১/২ শতাংশ এবং ৪৯৬ দাগের ৬ শতাংশ একুনে ৪১ এবং ১/২ শতাংশ জমিতে চিরস্থায়ী নিষেধাজ্ঞার প্রার্থনা করেছেন বাদীর দাখিলী প্রদ: ৫ চিহিত RS ৩১৪ নং খতিয়ানের সই মুহরি নকল পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে ৪৯৫ দাগে রেকর্ডভূক্ত মোট জমির পরিমান ৬০ শতাংশ, এরকাতে ৩৫ এবং ১/২ শতাংশ হচ্ছে নালিশী জমি বাদীর দাবীকৃত জমি দাগের অংশ বিশেষ হলে ও আর্জিত দাগের মোট জমিতে উক্ত আংশিক জমির অবস্থান নকশা যোগে প্রদর্শন করা হয়নি। তাছাড়া দাবীকৃত ৪৯৫ ও ৪৯৬ দাগের জমির অবস্থান সম্পর্কে কোন বর্ণনা সাক্ষ্য সূত্রে পাওয়া যায়না। ফলে নালিশি জমি অস্পষ্ট বিবেচিত হয়। (৯নং পৃষ্ঠা) অস্পষ্ট জমি বাবদ নিষেধাজ্ঞার আদেশ অকার্যকর হবার সম্ভাবনা আছে।

বাদী নালিশী জমিতে তার দখলের প্রমাণ স্বরুপ দাখিলী প্রর্দশনী ৭(ক) চিহ্নিত খাজনার দাখিলা পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় উহা একটি ৪৯৩ বি খতিয়ানভূক্ত ৩৫৯,৩৬০ ও ৪২৬ নং দাগভূক্ত জমির খাজনার দাখিলা যা নালিশী জমিভূক্ত নয়। বাদীর মৌখিক সাক্ষ্য সূত্রে দখলের প্রমাণ জেরায় ভিন্নরূপ প্রমাণিত হয়না।”

13. The aforesaid findings of the trial court established that the plaintiff apparently could able to prove title over the property by some documents but the plaintiff could not prove exclusive possession in the suit land and the schedule to the plaint is vague and indefinite and, as such, no decree of permanent injunction can be passed on a vague schedule.

14. With the above findings the suit was dismissed.

15. The appellate court also in its judgment concurrently found that the schedule to the plaint is vague and indefinite but found title of the plain- tiff only in 0.15 sataks of land in place of 40 sataks found by the trial court, Both the courts below concurrently observed that though the plaintiff in the plaint categorically given a chain of documents of title since 1942 but those documents have not been as marked exhibits in due process of law for which both the courts below came to a finding that the plaintiff could not properly prove his title in the suit property, In a suit for permanent injunction the paramount consideration is possession of the plaintiff in the suit land but both the courts below instead of giving emphasis on that point most erroneously put stress mainly on the title of the plaintiff. The appellate court found title of the plaintiff in 0.15 decimals of land only whereas the trial court found title in 0.40 decimals of land. The appellate court failed to assign any reason why it disagreed with the findings of the trial court on that finding.

16. From a perusal of the plaint, evidences on record both oral and documentary as contained in the lower court records this Court finds that the plaintiff submitted a series of registered deed before the trial court which have not been exhibited in accordance with law and both the courts below failed to give emphasis on the issue of possession of the plaintiff as well as of the defendant in the suit land.

<u>17. It is true that in the schedule to the plaint the property has not been well defined. For such defect in the plaint the petitioner could not be deprived of getting relief. It appears that CS Plot No. 359 contains 111 sataks of land. The plaintiff in suit did not mention CS Plot No, 359 divided into how many RS plots but in the plaint .only given RS Plot No, 495 which .contains only 60 sataks of land. It is also true that the petitioner did not claim the entire property covered by RS plot No, 495. It is obvious that the plaintiff has claimed part .of the RS plot No. 495 and CS plot No, 359. The petitioner ought to have given definite and specific boundary in which portion of the plot he is in possession by giving a sketch map to the plain.</u>

<u>18. From perusal .of the judgment of both the courts below I find that in deciding the case of the plaintiff both the courts below differently found title of the plaintiff in the suit land which contradicts each other, The question of possession in the suit land has not at all discussed by the courts below on the basis of evidences on record; Mere mistake in the schedule to the plaint a party should not suffer and should not be deprived of getting relief as prayed for, From the facts and circumstances of the case, I find that the documents submitted by the plaintiff has' not been properly marked as exhibits and the evidences have not been properly appreciated in its true perspective.</u>

<u>19. This being the situation, I think that the plaintiff should be given. a chance for making proper prayers by way of amendment of the plaint and also adduce evidences in support of his claim and in that situation, the defendants also shall be at liberty to file additional written statement and necessary documents in support 'of their claim. Accordingly, I think that justice will be met if the case is sent back on remand to the trial court for fresh trial affording sufficient opportunities to the parties to place their respective cases and get the plaint amended if so advised.</u>

20. In the result, the rule is made absolute however there will be no order as to costs. The impugned judgments and decrees passed by both the courts below are hereby set aside. The case is sent back on remand to the trial court for fresh trial and disposal within a shortest possible time preferably within 6(six) months from the date of the judgment of this Court:

21. Communicate a copy of this judgment to the Court concerned.

Send down the lower court records at once.

End.
